Revolution, Prison, Exile: Teofilo Ruiz on Leaving Cuba
description: Historian Teofilo Ruiz joins us to talk about his political engagement in Cuba. As a teenager in San Francisco de Paula, a town outside Havana, Ruiz joined the uprising against Fulgencio Batista. He then broke with the Castro government that replaced him, and in the run-up to the Bay of Pigs he found himself in jail. He left for Miami in 1961 with three changes of clothing, forty-five dollars, a box of Cuban cigars to sell, and a Spanish translation of Jacob Burckhardt’s A History of Greek Civilization , and went on to become one of the most celebrated historians and teachers in the country. Ruiz joins us to look back on the risks and disillusionments of his political life, and on the roots of the continuing tension between the U.S. and Cuba. A complimentary reception follows the program.

description: Tickets Haruko Tanaka (b. Queens, NY, 1974; d. October 2019) was a Los Angeles–based artist, photographer, graphic designer, and filmmaker engaged in social practice. Born in the United States, she was raised in England and Japan. Tanaka earned a B.A. in Fine Art from the University of Southern California in 1997 and an M.F.A. in Photography and Media Art from the California Institute of the Arts in 2003. Her visual work was exhibited widely at venues such as the Library Foundation of Los Angeles, the Japanese American National Museum, the Museum of Modern Art, CUE Art Foundation, the Torrance Art Museum, and the Armory Center for the Arts. She also screened her films internationally, including at the Rotterdam International Film Festival and the Asian American International Film Festival.
